basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Covers one taxpayer, tax type, jurisdiction and period from return preparation to assessment and dispute.
Keeps transmission receipt, filing acceptance, self-assessment and authority assessment as separate states.
Differs from the tax account, which accumulates liabilities and payments across periods.
Differs from payment, refund and penalty records, which are linked but not owned.

may: Assemble a draft return from source records with lineage.
Run calculation and validation rules and report errors.
Track deadlines, acknowledgements and authority correspondence.
Compare the filed position with the authority assessment and list differences.
mustNot: Give tax advice or choose a tax position on the taxpayer's behalf.
Sign a declaration or file a return.
Initiate tax payments or accept an assessment.
Waive or let lapse an appeal right.
Disclose taxpayer data beyond the permitted purpose.
requiresHuman: Accepting an assessment or launching an appeal.

considerations: Errors can create penalties, interest or loss of benefits for the taxpayer, often a private person.
Tax data is confidential by law in most jurisdictions.
Deadlines for appeals are strict, so silent delays can remove legal rights.

items: A tax case names a taxpayer reference, a tax type, a jurisdiction, a period, a return and its submission and assessment state.
Often confused with the tax account, a payment, a tax audit case or a tax registration.
Late or missing filing causing penalties.
Receipt taken as acceptance, hiding a rejected return.
Duplicate submission of the same return.
XBRL 2.1 for tax and financial reporting taxonomies.
OECD Standard Audit File for Tax (SAF-T).
HMRC Making Tax Digital VAT API.
W3C XML Signature for signed submissions.
